\mathbb T^{\rm cl}_k\,\mathbb T^{\rm cl}_{h-k}=\frac{\sinh u-i\sin\gamma_k}{\sinh u+i\sin\gamma_k}=\frac1{f_{k/h}(u)} ,
$$
and continued to $\theta-\frac{i\pi}2$ this gives the delay of a folded soliton,
$$
z_kz_{h-k}=\frac{\cosh u+\sin\gamma_k}{\cosh u-\sin\gamma_k} .
$$
For $2k\ne h$ it is finite and positive for real rapidities, so folded solitons are delayed or advanced and keep their charge. For $2k=h$ it is $\coth^2\frac u2$, which has a pole at $u=0$. Robertson [-@robertson2014a, Sec. 3.1] found the condition $\sigma_2=\pm\sigma_1$ and the reality of the delay from the solitons themselves; the linear waves show both in two lines. For $a_2^{(1)}\to a_2^{(2)}$, $\gamma_1=\frac\pi3$, and $z_1z_2$ is the delay $z_1$ of the Tzitzéica defect of @sec-type-two-atft, in its sector $e^{\hat\lambda}\to1$, as a function of $\theta-\theta_d$. We have not matched the defect parameters of the two descriptions; when they fold, Corrigan and Zambon [-@cz2009b, Sec. 5] replace their $\sigma$ by $1/(\sqrt2\sigma)$. All of this is checked in `code/defect_fused_boundary.py`.

## Reality and the defect {#sec-defect-theta}

In the bulk the antilinear map $\Theta:\vec\phi\mapsto-\bar{\vec\phi}$ maps solutions of the imaginary-coupling theory to solutions (@sec-theta-classical). @prp-boundary-theta showed that a boundary respects it exactly when its parameters are real. For a defect, $\Theta$ acts on both fields.

::: {#prp-defect-theta}
## The antilinear symmetry with a defect
**[Theorem]** For both types of massive $a_r^{(1)}$ defect at imaginary coupling, with $\beta\ne0$ and $\sigma\in\mathbb C^\times$,
$$
\overline{\mathcal B_d(\vec\phi,\vec\psi;\sigma)}=\mathcal B_d(-\bar{\vec\phi},-\bar{\vec\psi};\bar\sigma)
$$
for all complex fields. Hence $\Theta:(\vec\phi,\vec\psi)\mapsto(-\bar{\vec\phi},-\bar{\vec\psi})$ maps solutions of the defect theory with parameter $\sigma$ to solutions with parameter $\bar\sigma$, and it is a symmetry if and only if $\sigma$ is real, that is $\theta_d\in\mathbb R+i\pi\mathbb Z$. Then $E+\mathcal B_d$ and $P+P_d$ of $\Theta\vec\phi$ are the complex conjugates of those of $\vec\phi$. At real coupling the same holds for plain complex conjugation, the form $\Theta$ takes there (@exr-theta-solutions).
:::

::: {.proof}
In $\mathcal B_d^{\rm imag}=-\frac m{\beta^2}\sum_j[\sigma(f_j-1)+\sigma^{-1}(g_j-1)]$ the matrices $\mathsf D$, $E$ are real, and conjugation sends $f_j(\vec\phi,\vec\psi)$ to $f_j(-\bar{\vec\phi},-\bar{\vec\psi})$ and likewise $g_j$. This gives the identity. Conjugating the defect conditions then shows that $\Theta$ of a solution with $\sigma$ solves them with $\bar\sigma$; the bulk is as in @sec-theta-classical. The functions $f_j-1$ and $g_j-1$ are linearly independent, so $\mathcal B_d(\cdot;\bar\sigma)=\mathcal B_d(\cdot;\sigma)$ only if $\bar\sigma=\sigma$. We checked the identity for $a_2^{(1)}$ and $a_3^{(1)}$, both types and both couplings, and the action on an $a_2^{(1)}$ soliton passing a defect with complex $\sigma$: its $\Theta$-image satisfies the conditions with $\bar\sigma$ to $10^{-15}$ and violates them with $\sigma$ (`code/defect_classical_an.py`).
:::

On solitons, $\Theta$ maps $(a,\theta,\xi)$ to $(\bar a,\bar\theta,\bar\xi)$ (-@eq-theta-data), and the delays transform accordingly, $z_{\bar a}(\bar\theta;\bar\theta_d)=\overline{z_a(\theta;\theta_d)}$ (@sec-defect-backlund-an). For real $\theta_d$ a soliton and its antisoliton are delayed by complex conjugate factors, as Corrigan and Zambon [-@cz2007, Sec. 2] noted. Real $\sigma$ includes the odd sector $\sigma\to-\sigma$ of sine-Gordon, $\theta_d\to\theta_d+i\pi$. Imaginary $\theta_d\notin i\pi\mathbb Z$, which @sec-sg-defect-spectrum needs for stable excited defects, breaks $\Theta$, as the Lee–Yang defects of @sec-defect-lee-yang do. The type-II potentials above have real coefficients when $\hat\sigma$ and $\cosh2\tau$ are real, and then $\Theta$, acting as complex conjugation on the rescaled fields and on $\hat\lambda$, is a symmetry (by hand). @sec-defect-reality uses @prp-defect-theta for the reality of the energies of solitons passing a defect.

## Exercises {#sec-defect-conditions-exercises}

::: {#exr-dc-energy}
Derive (-@eq-defect-conditions) from (-@eq-defect-action), and show that $E+\mathcal B_d$ is conserved for any $\mathcal B_d$. Conversely, start from conditions $\partial_x\vec\phi=A\partial_t\vec\phi+B\partial_t\vec\psi+\vec X$, $\partial_x\vec\psi=C\partial_t\vec\phi+D\partial_t\vec\psi+\vec Y$ with constant matrices, and show that a modified energy is conserved only if $C=B^{\mathsf T}$, $A$ and $D$ are antisymmetric, and $\vec X$, $\vec Y$ are gradients of one function [@cz2009a, eq. (2.6)].
:::

::: {#exr-dc-d-matrix}
Prove the properties of $\mathsf D$ listed after (-@eq-d-matrix): $\mathsf D\vec\alpha_j=2(\vec\lambda_j-\vec\lambda_{j+1})$, $\mathsf D+\mathsf D^{\mathsf T}=2$, $\mathsf D=2(1-\pi)^{-1}$, $\mathsf D^{\mathsf T}\vec\alpha_j=-\mathsf D\vec\alpha_{j-1}$, and $\mathsf D=1+i\cot\frac{\pi k}h$ on the eigenvectors of $\pi$. Show that $\mathsf D^{\mathsf T}=2(1-\pi^{-1})^{-1}$, and that the reflection $\vec\alpha_j\to\vec\alpha_{-j}$ of the diagram conjugates $\mathsf D$ into $\mathsf D^{\mathsf T}$. Deduce that a soliton of species $a$ passing the mirror defect is delayed as a soliton of species $h-a$ passing the original one.
:::

::: {#exr-dc-scan}
Carry out the scan of @prp-ar-only by hand for small diagrams. (a) Show that every automorphism of $d_4^{(1)}$, $b_n^{(1)}$ and the twisted algebras of rank 2 fixes a node. (b) For $c_3^{(1)}$, show that the reversal of the chain fixes no node but fixes the vector $\vec\alpha_0+\vec\alpha_3$, so that $1-P$ is singular. Generalize: an automorphism with more than one orbit never works. (c) For $a_4^{(1)}$ and $P=\pi^2$, compute $\vec\alpha_i\cdot\mathsf D\vec\alpha_j$ and find the forbidden cross terms. (d) For $a_1^{(1)}$, show that the exchange of the two nodes gives $\mathsf D=1$ and (-@eq-sg-defect-potential).
:::

::: {#exr-dc-cot}
Prove $\cot a\cot b+\cot b\cot c+\cot c\cot a=1$ for $a+b+c\equiv0$ mod $\pi$. Show that $A(\vec u,\vec u,\vec u)=2\sum_k(\vec\mu_k\cdot\vec u)^3$ solves [@bcz2004b, eq. (5.5)] with $B=1-\mathsf D$ (their density (5.2) contains $\frac13A$), and that $A(\mathsf D\vec v)^3+A(\mathsf D^{\mathsf T}\vec v)^3=0$. For $a_2^{(1)}$ write out $A(\mathsf D\vec v)^3$ and check that it is not zero.
:::

::: {#exr-dc-lax}
For $a_1^{(1)}$ in the two-dimensional representation, with $H=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)/\sqrt2$, verify that $L_d=e^{-bH\psi/2}(1+\frac\sigma\lambda\sigma_x)e^{bH\phi/2}$ satisfies $\partial_tL_d=L_da_t(\psi)-a_t(\phi)L_d$ on the defect conditions (-@eq-sg-defect-conditions). Using the boost property of @sec-lax-pair, show that the coefficients of $\lambda^{-n}$ at $\lambda\to\infty$ have spin $-n$ and those of $\lambda^n$ at $\lambda\to0$ spin $+n$. Show that the first defect contribution at $\lambda\to\infty$ is proportional to $\sigma$ and the first at $\lambda\to0$ to $\sigma^{-1}$, as for $E-P$ and $E+P$ in @prp-sg-defect-momentum.
:::

::: {#exr-dc-bracket}
For $a_1^{(1)}$, show from (-@eq-dc-defect-bracket) that $\{\phi(0),\psi(0)\}=-1$ for type I$_-$. Using $r(z)$ of @prp-sklyanin with $h=2$, verify $\{L_d(\lambda_1)\overset\otimes,L_d(\lambda_2)\}=[r(\lambda_1/\lambda_2),L_d(\lambda_1)\otimes L_d(\lambda_2)]$ entry by entry. What changes for type I$_+$?
:::

::: {#exr-dc-delay}
For the $a_r$ soliton, show that $f_j=\tau_{j+1}\tau'_{j-1}/(\tau_j\tau'_j)$ and $g_j=\tau_{j-1}\tau'_j/(\tau_j\tau'_{j-1})$, where $\tau'_j$ are the $\tau$-functions of $\vec\psi$. Substitute into the defect conditions for $a_2^{(1)}$ and derive (-@eq-dc-ar-delay). Prove the twisted Bianchi form, the identity for $z_az_{\bar a}$, and $z_{\bar a}(\bar\theta;\bar\theta_d)=\overline{z_a(\theta;\theta_d)}$.
:::

::: {#exr-dc-type-two}
From (-@eq-dc-type-two) derive the type-II defect conditions and show that $E+\mathcal D$ is conserved. Verify that the sine-Gordon $f$ and $g$ satisfy $\frac12(f_qg_\Lambda-f_\Lambda g_q)=V(\phi)-V(\psi)$ in the rescaled variables, and find the static values of $e^{\hat\lambda}$ when the jump is even and when it is odd. Show that the two delays of @prp-type-ii-momentum are $z_{\rm I_-}(\theta;\theta_d+\tau)z_{\rm I_-}(\theta;\theta_d-\tau)$ and $z_{\rm odd}(\theta;\theta_d+\tau)z_{\rm odd}(\theta;\theta_d-\tau)$, and that they are inverse to each other.
:::

## Notes and references {#sec-defect-conditions-notes}

Bowcock, Corrigan and Zambon introduced the Lagrangian jump defect for sine-Gordon theory and showed that its conditions are a frozen Bäcklund transformation [-@bcz2004]. They then extended it to affine Toda theory, constructed the defect matrix by overlapping Lax pairs, found that only $a_r^{(1)}$ admits a type-I defect, and recovered the defect from the Bäcklund condition [-@bcz2004b]. Corrigan and Zambon computed the delays of $a_r$ solitons and the $a_2$ transmission matrix [-@cz2007], made momentum conservation the organizing principle [-@cz2009a], introduced type-II defects with the Tzitzéica example [-@cz2009b], and related the defects to infinite-dimensional representations of Borel subalgebras [-@cz2011]. Robertson folded fused $a_r$ defects [-@robertson2014a] and introduced defect fusing rules [-@robertson2014b]. Bristow and Bowcock generalized type-II defects to several auxiliary fields and found them for four series of algebras [-@bristow_bowcock2017], and Bristow constructed their Lax matrices [-@bristow2017]. Habibullin and Kundu gave a lattice-regularized r-matrix treatment of the sine-Gordon defect [-@habibullin_kundu2008], Avan and Doikou the sewing-condition approach [-@avan_doikou2012a; -@avan_doikou2012b], Doikou its $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ version [-@doikou2014], and Caudrelier the systematic and multisymplectic treatments [-@caudrelier2008; -@caudrelier2015; -@caudrelier_kundu2015]. Penati and Polvara studied the quantum conservation laws [-@penati_polvara2019]. The scan of @prp-ar-only, the survival of both chiralities with the general cancellation and the explicit $\mathcal B_{\pm2}$ of @prp-spin-two, the bracket (-@eq-dc-defect-bracket) for independent defect values with the Sklyanin relation of @prp-defect-involution, its proof for $a_1^{(1)}$ with the uniqueness of the r-matrix, the twisted Bianchi form (-@eq-dc-ar-delay), and @prp-defect-theta are stated here. So are the general solution (-@eq-dc-halves) of condition 2 with the light-cone form (-@eq-dc-lightcone), the neighbour argument in the form that completes the proof of @prp-ar-only, the components (-@eq-dc-components), @prp-dc-types with its consequence for the spin-two charges, and @prp-dc-gauge. In @prp-sg-spin-three the closed form of $\mathcal D_{-3}$ is Caudrelier's [-@caudrelier2008, eq. (3.28)], found in light-cone coordinates; its form for a defect at rest, with both chiralities, and the charges stored by a jump are stated here. Habibullin and Kundu's [-@habibullin_kundu2008, Sec. 5] lattice defect operator has the algebraic structure of the $a_1^{(1)}$ defect matrix. Penati and Polvara [-@penati_polvara2019, Sec. 3] related the kinetic terms of the two types; we did not find @prp-dc-types itself in the sources we checked, which include the papers of Robertson [-@robertson2014a; -@robertson2014b] and of Bristow and Bowcock [-@bristow_bowcock2017]. We did not find the cancellation of the spin-two obstruction in the sources we checked, but have not searched the later literature exhaustively.

Corrections and clarifications to the sources made in this chapter:

- Both spin-$\pm2$ charges of $a_r^{(1)}$ survive a type-I defect of either type, contrary to @bcz2004b [Sec. 5] and @penati_polvara2019 [App. B]. The obstruction [@bcz2004b, eq. (5.11)] vanishes identically: their inference from $\mathsf D=2-\mathsf D^{\mathsf T}$ [@bcz2004b, eq. (3.20)] to a nonzero (5.11) overlooks that the cubic invariant couples only Fourier modes with $k_1+k_2+k_3\equiv0$ mod $h$, on which the cotangent identity cancels the two terms. The cubic terms of @penati_polvara2019 [eq. (B.4)] vanish for the same reason. The two types differ in their Borel subalgebra, not in a surviving charge.
- In @bcz2004b [eq. (5.43)] the matrix is printed as $2\sum_i\vec\lambda_i(\vec\lambda_i-\vec\lambda_{i+1})^{\mathsf T}$, the transpose of their (3.28); with their $E$ of (5.42), $1-E$ is the matrix of (3.28).
- [@cz2007, eq. (2.21)]: for a self-conjugate soliton their (2.20) gives $z=-\coth\frac{\theta-\eta}2$, not $+\coth\frac{\theta-\eta}2$; the sign is that of the sine-Gordon delay (-@eq-sg-delay) and of @bcz2004b [eq. (6.2)].
- [@cz2009b, eq. (4.4)]: the defect field in the sector of the delay $z_1$ is $e^{\lambda_1}=-\frac1{\sqrt2\cosh\tau}\frac{(1+E_0)(1+z_1E_0)}{(1-\rho E_0)(1-\tilde\rho E_0)}$; the printed form, with the opposite overall sign and $1+\rho E_0$, $1+\tilde\rho E_0$, violates the defect conditions (3.3). Their $z_1$ is the sector $e^\lambda\to-1/(\sqrt2\cosh\tau)$. For imaginary $E_0$ and real parameters their (4.5) becomes $e^{2i\operatorname{Im}\lambda_1}=\frac{1+E_0}{1-E_0}\,\frac{1+z_1E_0}{1-z_1E_0}\,\frac{1+\rho E_0}{1-\rho E_0}\,\frac{1+\tilde\rho E_0}{1-\tilde\rho E_0}$, with the last two factors inverted. The phase of $e^{\lambda_1}$ therefore winds by $2\pi$ when $\rho$ and $\tilde\rho$ are both positive, not when both are negative as stated after their (4.5) (by hand from the corrected (4.4), which is checked in `code/defect_classical_an.py`).
- [@cz2009b, eq. (3.7)]: $1/\sigma$ multiplies both terms of $f$, as their (4.6) requires. Their (4.11) for $z_2$ is the complex conjugate of the $z_2$ of their (4.9), i.e. their $z_3$.
